name: surface
description: Generic visual box with elevation and configurable padding, optionally capped at one of the shared measure widths

changes.note: Elevation variants now map to the guaranteed semantic ramp: flat uses the page background, raised/default use surface-1 and its border, and overlay uses surface-2 and its border.

BREAKING: data-max is re-expressed over the shared measure tokens (task 0.8-06). Its 1.x values were five hardcoded pixel widths named after the breakpoint canon — sm 640px, md 768px, lg 1024px, xl 1280px, 2xl 1400px — so data-max="lg" read as "at the lg tier" when it meant "1024px wide", which is exactly the multi-ladder drift task 0.8-01 set out to kill. The values are now the same vocabulary the container primitive speaks, resolving to the same tokens: narrow (--measure-narrow, 32rem), content (--measure-content, 48rem), wide (--measure-wide, 72rem), prose (--measure-prose, 65ch) and the unchanged full. Migration: data-max="sm" → "narrow"; "md" → "content" (768px = 48rem, the one value that is preserved exactly); "lg"/"xl"/"2xl" → "wide", or a container around the surface when the old pixel width was load-bearing. The cap is also logical now (max-inline-size, not max-width), so it flips under RTL. Newly declared, previously present in the CSS but absent from the manifest: data-max and data-align-text — nothing generated from manifests knew either attribute existed.

max.description: Caps the surface at one of the shared measure tokens and centres it. Same vocabulary as the container primitive's data-measure — when the measure is the only thing wanted, reach for container instead; this is for a box that needs the elevation too.

align-text.description: Text alignment for the whole surface. Logical: `right` maps to text-align: end, so it flips under RTL.

a11y.notes: Layout-only primitive; no semantic role required. Use landmark roles on the content inside when appropriate.
